connector.modeled: 50 ohm port at board edge y=-13 (reference plane); connector body not modeled

feed: microstrip_inset_edge, w = 3.02 mm, y0 = 2.0 mm, g = 0.5 mm, entering at y = -13 along +y through the bottom flat side
changed_vs_base.patch_polygon: regular hexagon, vertices at 0, 60 ... 300 deg (flat sides toward +-y, vertices toward +-x), circumradius 5.2 mm, with an inset notch of width 4.02 mm and depth 2.0 mm on the bottom flat side (non-convex, 10 vertices)

rationale: Primera iteracion del elemento P03 (parche hexagonal con ranura hexagonal central) con la misma linea microstrip de 50 ohm, el mismo inset (y0 = 2.0 mm, g = 0.5 mm) y el mismo puerto de borde que P02_MS1. El hexagono de designs.py (radio 0.53 W = 6.05 mm) no estaba dimensionado para resonar; aqui r = 5.2 mm se elige con dos estimaciones que acotan el canal y con una restriccion de fabricacion. Orientacion: la orientacion natural de designs.hexagon (vertices a 0 grados) deja un lado plano hacia -y, de 5.2 mm, donde cabe la muesca (4.02 mm) con 0.59 mm de cobre a cada lado; con un vertice hacia -y la muesca no cabria hasta unos 1.5 mm de profundidad. El modo excitado es el analogo TM11 con campo maximo a lo largo de y (entre lados planos, distancia 9.01 mm), simetrico respecto de x = 0; la linea centrada solo acopla el modo simetrico, y la degeneracion con el modo a lo largo de x se rompe por el hexagono y la muesca. La ranura hexagonal (r = 1.1 mm, del mismo designs.py) cae en el centro, donde el campo electrico del modo es nulo y la corriente es maxima, por lo que carga inductivamente el modo y baja algo su frecuencia (no estimado); no se escala para mantener la trazabilidad con designs.py. Resonancia esperada, cualitativamente: un modo principal TM11-like a lo largo de y cerca del canal, con frecuencia entre ~7.7 y ~8.2 GHz segun la estimacion que se use, menos la carga de la ranura y de la muesca; el hexagono no es un circulo, asi que no se espera segundo modo util dentro del canal. Todo es GEOMETRY_ONLY.

inputs.bias_source: P01 FDTD fr 7.47 GHz / 7.9872 GHz (variants/README.md, P01_R1 step 2)

line_50ohm.method: Hammerstad-Jensen (1980) microstrip analysis, thickness-corrected, solved by bisection for Z0 = 50 ohm
formulas: thickness: du1 = (t/(pi*h))*ln(1+4e/((t/h)*coth^2(sqrt(6.517*u)))) ; du_r = 0.5*(1+1/cosh(sqrt(er-1)))*du1 ; u_r = u + du_r

result.cross_check: Hammerstad 1975 synthesis (w/h>2 formula, t=0) gives w/h = 1.913, i.e. 3.061 mm, equal to the t=0 bisection (3.062 mm); the 35 um copper narrows the line by 0.045 mm

line_50ohm.dispersion_note: Quasi-static value. Getsinger dispersion (G = 0.6+0.009*Z0, fp = Z0/(2*mu0*h) = 12.4 GHz) raises eps_eff to ~3.64-3.67 in 7.74-8.24 GHz, which shifts Z0 by a few percent (sign and size not evaluated here). Not corrected: the FDTD includes it and the port impedance is a reference, not a design result. FR4 eps_r itself is provisional.
line_50ohm.uncertainty: +-3 % in Z0 expected from the Hammerstad-Jensen formula and +-5-10 % from provisional eps_r; the real board fabricator's etch tolerance on w is not consulted.

notch_gap.justification: 0.5 mm is the smallest gap the owner/orchestrator allows as 'min distance' in this round and is applied uniformly to notch gap, U-slot width and all clearances so the layout has one minimum feature size. No fabricator rule was consulted and none is invented: whether 0.5 mm (and a copper tab of 0.59 mm in P03) is acceptable must be confirmed with the chosen PCB house. Electromagnetically g only weakly changes R(y0) for narrow gaps; a larger g is safer for etching but adds notch inductance and moves more current path, so g is kept at the minimum rather than inflated.
notch_gap.mesh_note: g = 0.5 mm is ~1.4 cells at the 'base' 0.35 mm xy mesh; em-solver needs local lines at the notch walls (g/3 or better) or the gap is not resolved.

inset_depth.law: R(y0) = R_edge*cos^2(pi*y0/L) (cavity model, y0 measured from the radiating edge along the resonant axis), target 50 ohm
inset_depth.uncertainty: R_edge comes from PROBE feeds. An inset microstrip feed sees a different edge conductance (fringing, notch, junction inductance of the notch gap), and the literature (Basilio et al. 2001, cited from memory, NOT checked here) reports that for narrow notches R_in(y0) falls closer to cos^4 than to cos^2. That alternative would require y0 = 1.48-1.65 mm instead of 2.02-2.23 mm. The first iteration is therefore a calibration point, not a matched design.
inset_depth.hexagon_axis: flat-to-flat 2*apothem = 9.007 mm along y; apothem 4.5033 mm
inset_depth.model_R(y0): Two versions: (i) cos^2 on the flat-to-flat length D = 9.007 mm: y0(50 ohm) = 2.38-2.63 mm for R_edge 110-135; (ii) circular-cavity Bessel TM11: R(y0) = R_edge*(J1(k*(apothem-y0)/a_e)/J1(k))^2 with k = 1.8412, a_e = 5.097 mm: y0(50 ohm) = 2.12-2.39 mm.
inset_depth.y0_choice: Same inset as P02_MS1 by instruction, to compare the two elements with the same feed. Both hexagon models give y0 for 50 ohm above 2.0 mm, so R at y0 = 2.0 mm is expected above 50 ohm in both cos^2/Bessel models: 54-66 ohm (Bessel) or 65-79 ohm (cos^2 on D); a cos^4-like law would lower it. R_edge of a hexagon is assumed equal to the rectangular probe-derived R_edge (not established).

computation.feed_line_geometry: Line = rectangle x in [-w/2, w/2], y in [-13, line_end_y]. The notch removes the patch between x = +-(w/2+g) from the radiating edge up to line_end_y, so the line touches the patch only along its end segment at y = line_end_y (width w). em-solver adds the line as a separate PEC polygon; the shared edge may need the same mesh line.
computation.port_note: Reference plane at y = -13 (board edge). The line between the port and the patch is a real part of the circuit (about 9 mm long), so phase of S11 includes it; |S11| is unaffected except for line loss and radiation. An openEMS MSL port (or an equivalent line-mode port) is more appropriate than a lumped port across the open end, to be decided by em-solver. The SMA body, its pin transition and any solder fillet are NOT modeled (no part reference).

radius_estimate.TM11_circular_cavity: fr = k*c/(2*pi*a_e*sqrt(eps_r)), k = 1.8412 ; a_e = a*sqrt(1 + (2h/(pi*a*eps_r))*(ln(pi*a/(2h)) + 1.7726)) (Garg/Bahl fringing formula, used as cited from memory)

estimate_B_with_P01_bias.note: The P01 plain patch resonated 6.5 % below its transmission-line prediction in FDTD (7.47 vs 7.9872 GHz). B scales a_e by the same factor 0.93525 (same procedure used for P01_R1), then solves a. It assumes the circular formula has the same bias as the Hammerstad rectangle formula, which is NOT established.

radius_estimate.choice: r = 5.2 mm: close to the midpoint of A and B (5.18 mm) and just above the fabrication constraint r >= 5.17 mm (see fabrication_constraint)

fr_at_r_5.2_GHz.note: These two bracket the channel (7.7376-8.2368 GHz) but are model arithmetic, not predictions; the central hex slot and the notch are NOT included and will lower fr further.

radius_estimate.fabrication_constraint: The notch (half-width w/2+g = 2.01 mm) must leave copper beside it on the bottom flat side of half-length r/2. Requiring >= 0.5 mm of copper strip measured perpendicular to the sloped side gives r/2 - 2.01 >= 0.5/sin(60 deg) = 0.577 mm -> r >= 5.17 mm. r = 5.2 mm leaves 0.59 mm of flat (a small copper tab; closest point to the wall is the vertex at 0.59 mm) and a wider strip above it.
radius_estimate.uncertainty: fr of the main mode: +-5 % or more (hexagon vs circle, bias transfer, slot and notch loading not included). It is more likely to end up BELOW f0 than above, since A and B are both unperturbed values and the hole and the notch add inductive loading.

computation.checks_script: scratchpad-only pure-python check; same checks reproducible from the polygon coordinates in this JSON.

manufacturability.min_feature_note: Notch gap and clearances >= 0.5 mm; copper tab between notch wall and outer vertex is 0.59 mm long. Not a verified fabricator capability.
manufacturability.hex_slot_note: The 1.1 mm radius hexagonal hole (side 1.1 mm) is small; the FDTD needs mesh cells <= ~0.3 mm over it, and its oblique edges are staircased in openEMS.

computation.uncertainty_summary: r from two model estimates with ~7 % spread; R at the inset: model dependent; hole effect unquantified.
